properties.decision:
RECORDED AS A MEASURED FIELD DEFECT PLUS AN OPEN QUESTION. Reported 2026-08-05 from a real session on `hxm_program`, Anthony's own working repo at NSLS-II. Nothing here is settled.

⭐ WHAT HAPPENED, AND IT IS AN ACCIDENT THE TOOL CAUSED RATHER THAN FAILED TO PREVENT. A session rooted at the repo root was told "this directory has no design yet" and offered only `reflow2_start_design`. TWO POPULATED GRAPHS EXISTED ONE AND TWO DIRECTORIES DOWN:

    ~/git_projects/hxm_program/.reflow2                      37bbd9a6e0e75369  "hxm_program"          minted 0.23.0 TODAY
    ~/git_projects/hxm_program/simulated_beamlines/.reflow2  8a9ce30fedd213e5  "simulated_beamlines"  minted 0.17.0
    ~/git_projects/hxm_program/simulated_beamlines/HEX/.reflow2  6771abb9b0683423  "HEX"              minted 0.22.1

The user believed the design lived at `simulated_beamlines`. By the time that surfaced, the agent HAD ALREADY MINTED A NEW ROOT GRAPH. The reporter's own summary: "One directory listing would have prevented the accidental third graph."

WHY THIS IS THE SEVERE ONE OF THE SIX FILED. Every other item in the report is friction — this one produced a WRONG ARTEFACT in the user's repository, silently, and the user did not learn of it until later. It is also the exact failure shape this project has been finding all week and naming in its own words: A GREEN OR CONFIDENT ANSWER FROM SOMETHING THAT NEVER LOOKED. `reflow2_check` reported OK over 20 artifacts it never swept ([BL-206]); the export-lineage guard reported nothing because it could not see `HEAD~1` ([BL-208]); `loop_status` reports `unsurfaced_gaps: 0` before `detect_gaps` has ever run (item 4 of this same report). "No design here" is that sentence again, addressed to a person deciding whether to create one.

AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE OTHERS IN ONE RESPECT: the other three report a state, and this one INVITES AN IRREVERSIBLE ACT on the strength of it. A design minted in the wrong place is not a bad reading; it is a fourth thing to reconcile.

THE SECOND HALF, WHICH THE REPORT COUPLES TO IT: SESSION BINDING. "The MCP server binds to the session's working directory. From a root-rooted session there is no way to write into the nested HEX graph — the user would have to open a session in that directory." Verified against this repo's own `.mcp.json`: the launcher is passed `--graph-path ./.reflow2/graph`, a RELATIVE path with NO ANCESTOR WALK. So which design you are editing is decided by where your shell happened to be. Also reported: choosing the new root graph "required a manual `/mcp` reconnect after `start_design`, because the running server predated the design and kept serving only `start_design`."

⚠️ THIS FALSIFIES ADVICE GIVEN THE SAME DAY, and the correction belongs on the record next to it. Asked how to structure exactly these repos, this agent answered that a single graph needs no restructuring because `Artifact.location` is an opaque string and reflow2 performs no file IO — so one graph could register artifacts across sibling repos. TRUE OF ARTIFACT LOCATIONS AND FALSE OF THE THING THAT MATTERS: with cwd-binding and no ancestor walk, "one graph" silently means "every session must start at the repo root", and a session opened one directory down does not find it — it offers to mint another. The advice was given from the schema and the doctrine (`dec:install-once-per-machine`) without checking the launcher. THE SAME METHOD ERROR AS THE `export_surface` CORRECTION AN HOUR EARLIER: an absence asserted from a description rather than read from the code.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) SCAN BEFORE OFFERING TO MINT — the reporter's own suggestion: "no design here, but 2 exist below: [paths, labels]. Use one of those, or really start fresh?" Cheapest, and it directly prevents the accident that occurred. Counter: reflow2 performs NO FILE IO by doctrine (`dec:agent-navigates-content`), so the scan cannot be reflow2's — it has to be the agent's, which makes this an instruction in the served surface rather than a tool, and instructions are weaker than a type system. That may be the honest answer rather than a weakness, but it should be chosen rather than defaulted to. (b) WALK ANCESTORS WHEN RESOLVING THE GRAPH PATH, the way git finds `.git`. Familiar and predictable; counter: it silently changes which design a session writes to based on cwd depth, which is the same class of surprise, and `--graph-path` is explicit today. (c) A GRAPH SELECTOR — "design tools take an optional graph ref, defaulting to the nearest `.reflow2`" (reporter's 2a). The largest, and it is the one that would also answer the nested-write problem. Counter: it makes every tool call carry an ambient target, and this project has been careful that a claim without a seat is refused rather than guessed (`dec:stateless-seat-handle`). (d) HOT-LOAD THE FULL SURFACE AFTER `start_design` (reporter's 2b) — narrower, fixes only the reconnect papercut, and is independent of the rest.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: `dec:install-once-per-machine` (the in-repo half is optional), `.mcp.json` passing a RELATIVE `--graph-path`, and the fact that three graphs of three different mint versions (0.17.0 / 0.22.1 / 0.23.0) now coexist in one repo with no stated compatibility policy — the report's item 6.

NOT CHECKED: whether `reflow2_start_design` could refuse, rather than warn, when a `.reflow2` exists below it. Refusing is stronger than reporting and may be right for an act this hard to undo.
properties.name: OPEN — "this directory has no design yet" is asserted without looking, and it minted a THIRD graph on a repo that already had two
properties.rationale:
Filed from a first-hand field report on Anthony's real work rather than from self-host, which is the second time in one day that pointing reflow2 at something it did not author produced a finding self-host could not. That pattern is now three-for-three ([BL-199], [BL-213], this) and is the strongest standing argument for keeping external use in rotation.

Recorded as its own node rather than as one of six backlog rows because it is categorically different from the other five: those are friction, this one CAUSED a wrong artefact in a user's repository and invited an irreversible act on the strength of an unchecked claim. Filing it beside "version skew is a papercut" would flatten that.

The falsified advice is written into the node deliberately. It was given today, confidently, from doctrine rather than from the launcher — and an agent reading this later needs to see that the one-graph recommendation rested on a fact nobody had checked, not just that it was incomplete.
